name: Notify a Slack channel when documents arrive in Folderit

nodes.name: Setup: Notify Slack about new Folderit files

parameters.content:
# Notify Slack about new Folderit files
For teams that need document arrival notifications. Retrieves current file details, optionally limits messages to one exact parent folder, escapes Slack mentions, and includes the audit UID for reconciliation. No document content is sent.

1. Install **n8n-nodes-folderit 0.4.0 or later**. [Setup guide](https://www.folderit.com/knowledge-base/connect-folderit-to-n8n/)
2. Select the Folderit OAuth2 credential and account in **New Folderit file**. Select the same credential in **Read new document details**.
3. In **Settings**, enter the same account UID and the Slack channel ID; optionally enter the exact folder UID. A blank folder means all accessible folders. Child folders are not included in an exact folder filter.
4. Connect a Slack OAuth2 credential in **Notify Slack channel** and invite the app to that channel. Test with a private test channel before activation.

# Scheduling and delivery limits
Activation establishes a new baseline. Upload a synthetic file AFTER activation, wait for a scheduled poll, and check the actual Slack message. Manual trigger tests preview recent events and can send historical notifications.

The trigger is polled every minute. Poll at least hourly; reconcile any interruption longer than 23 hours or an exceeded scan limit. Quiet polling persistence was tested locally on n8n 2.42.5 with durable polling enabled; a fresh Cloud run remains unverified.

Duplicate audit UIDs are removed within one execution. This is not a durable cross-execution ledger or exactly-once delivery. Downstream failures/replays can repeat messages. An uncertain Slack response needs a channel check before retrying. A deleted/inaccessible file stops execution; inspect and reconcile the event rather than silently discarding it.

For Microsoft Teams, replace only the final Slack node with Microsoft Teams / Channel Message / Create and map its message to the prepared text. Teams needs its own credential, team/channel and a separate end-to-end test.
